name: Basilisk, Badalischio
body:
Badalischio CR
6

The head of this man-sized serpent is crowned with circling horn-like projections, and its eyes are lit from within with a red glow.

XP 2,400
NE Medium magical beast
Init +5; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 11, flat-footed 18 (+1 Dex, +8 natural)
hp 65 (7d10+31)
Fort +9, Ref +4, Will +3

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 40 ft. (good), swim 30 ft.
Melee bite +11 (1d8+4 plus poison), gore +9 (1d6+1)
Special Attacks breath weapon (15-ft. cone, 6d6 acid, Reflex half DC 16, usable every 1d4 rounds), paralyzing gaze (1d4 rounds, 30-ft., DC 13), poison (bite), pounce

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 13, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 11
Base Atk +7; CMB +10; CMD 21 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Improved Initiative, Multiattack, Skill Focus (Stealth), Toughness
Skills Fly +12, Perception +9, Stealth +12, Swim +11; Racial Modifiers +4 Fly, +4 Stealth Languages -SQ Amphibious

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Paralyzing Gaze (Su)

Become paralyzed for 1d4 rounds, 30 feet, Fortitude DC 13 negates. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Poison (Ex)

Bite injury; save Fort DC 11; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d2 Con; cure 1 save.

ECOLOGY

Environment any forest and fresh water
Organization solitary, pair, or colony (3-6)
Treasure double

These adaptable predators can attack from the land, water, or air, as their preference dictates. Badalischios are commonly found in forested regions near large bodies of fresh water.

They can be found lairing in caves on hillsides, hollow trees, or in the beds of lakes or rivers. A typical badalischio is between 7 and 9 feet in length, with a wingspan of about 14 feet. Their scales have a reticulated pattern of green, brown, and gold.

Badalischios are attracted to things that glitter and shine, often decorating their lairs with treasure. With no acumen for telling the value of objects, this “treasure” may simply be glass or cheap metals as often as things of actual value. However, the badalischio has enough intelligence to understand that other creatures value such things, and often uses them as lures to attract prey.
